node.title: Support-distance scalar descent for Reed-Solomon lists
node.statement: Let E/F_q have degree r and let the evaluation domain lie in F_q. Put t=n-a, g=a-k+1, N_r=(q^r-1)/(q-1), and H_r=(q^(r-1)-1)/(q-1). If LtH_r<gN_r, then the existence of an E-valued RS list of size L at agreement a is equivalent to the existence of an F_q-valued list of size L. Thus the extension and base upper predicates at threshold L-1 are equivalent. The theorem does not prove either upper predicate; the upstream Mersenne-31 quartic specialization uses target 2^-100, not the local 2^-128 target.
